The toolkit collects reusable resources for criminology pages: definitions, methods, modelling steps, and checks for moving from a topic to a clear explanation.

It is meant to support the rest of the criminology section rather than replace it.

## Toolkit map

```{mermaid}
flowchart TD
    A[Criminology Toolkit] --> B[Glossary]
    A --> C[Methods Map]
    A --> D[Modeling Checklist]

    B --> B1[Core terms]
    B --> B2[Measurement concepts]
    B --> B3[Theory labels]

    C --> C1[Descriptive questions]
    C --> C2[Causal questions]
    C --> C3[Mechanism questions]
    C --> C4[Prediction questions]

    D --> D1[Actors]
    D --> D2[Choices]
    D --> D3[Information]
    D --> D4[Payoffs]
    D --> D5[Timing]
```

## How to use the toolkit

Use the toolkit when a page feels unclear.

If the problem is vocabulary, use the [Glossary](glossary.qmd).

If the problem is research design, use the [Methods Map](methods-map.qmd).

If the problem is model structure, use the [Modeling Checklist](modeling-checklist.qmd).

```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
    A[Unclear page] --> B{What is unclear?}
    B -->|Terms| C[Glossary]
    B -->|Evidence or design| D[Methods Map]
    B -->|Actors and incentives| E[Modeling Checklist]
```

## From topic to analysis

A criminology page should usually move through this chain:

```{mermaid}
flowchart TD
    A[Topic] --> B[Definition]
    B --> C[Mechanism]
    C --> D[Evidence or measurement]
    D --> E[Institutional context]
    E --> F[Model or framework]
    F --> G[Policy implication]
```

The toolkit supports this chain by making each step more explicit.
